initiative.title: PR compare mode
initiative.summary: Compare two git commits (PR base vs head) in srcly: focused before/after tree and dependency graph views limited to changed files by default, with per-metric better/worse deltas, all deterministic from disk and git.
initiative.next_action: Review and squash-merge the stacked PRs in order: #37 docs → #38 CLI → #39 table → #40 treemap → #41 graph; then retire or extend the initiative

claims.statement: Compare metrics and dependencies between two git commits, typically before/after a PR.
Strong left/right (before/after) views of the tree view and the dependency graph.
The user can tell whether things got better or worse.
Views are truncated/focused to only changed files by default.
The diagram is generated deterministically from disk and diff with no LLM in the path.
Unchanged nodes appear in the same positions on both sides so before/after connectivity is comparable.
Widely used changed components should be surfaced as such rather than lighting up everything.
Change islands / PR splittability, ripple-frontier, and route/component lenses are longer-horizon ideas.
Show changed files with +/- line counts grouped by folder (memo notes GitHub file tree lacks per-file magnitude).
Show per-metric deltas plus a neutral net line; no overall verdict.
Side-by-side treemaps are in v1 alongside the Explorer compare table.
Default head is the working tree; base and head must be configurable to arbitrary commits early.

shape.appetite: One compare mode over existing tree, metrics, and dependency graph. No new analyzers, call graph, or GitHub API.
shape.problem: Judging a PR's structural effect today means scanning two checkouts by hand and eyeballing two full-repo views.
shape.recommended_shape: Snapshot both commits via detached git worktrees, scan with the normal pipeline cached by SHA, diff server-side into one compare payload, and render focused before/after Explorer and a union-layout dependency graph drawn twice.

success_moves.move: Cache scans by commit SHA instead of mtime fingerprint.
success_moves.benefit: Commits are immutable; repeated compares are instant and the fingerprint walk is skipped.

success_moves.move: Pure Python compare module (two trees + two graphs + git name-status -> payload) shared by UI and future CLI.
success_moves.benefit: One definition of better/worse; fixture-testable in pytest with no git or UI.

success_moves.move: Union-graph layout computed once, filtered per side.
success_moves.benefit: Guarantees stable positions without a new layout engine; reuses pure grid layout.

success_moves.move: First proof is CLI JSON on srcly's own history before any UI.
success_moves.benefit: Proves snapshot path resolution and delta correctness, the riskiest backend pieces, cheaply.

success_moves.move: Compare mode is a separate view; single-scan view untouched.
success_moves.benefit: Rollback is removing an entry point; no regression risk to the main view.

first_proof.question: Can srcly snapshot two commits, scan both with correct path resolution, and produce a correct change set with metric deltas and dependency edge diffs at acceptable cost?
first_proof.artifact: CLI JSON for aa3ed35^ -> aa3ed35 on srcly; rename fixture in pytest
first_proof.decision_rule: Deltas match hand-checked sample and both scans < ~2x a normal scan -> build UI on payload. Path resolution breaks in snapshots -> switch to git archive into a mirrored path first.

rabbit_holes: Treemap union layout with max-weight tiles: verify readability when many files are added or removed
Rename matching for symbols (not just files)
Hub files lighting up the whole graph
Working-tree side uses fingerprint cache while commit sides use SHA cache
Scan time for two full scans on large repos

dependencies.name: git CLI (worktree add/remove, diff --name-status -M, merge-base)
dependencies.strategy: Real local git on srcly repo; pure compare module tested with fixture trees and name-status text.

implementation.fast_local_loop: cd server && uv run pytest tests/test_compare*.py (real throwaway git repo in tmp_path); cd client && pnpm test for union layouts

cut_line: more than two refs / branch over time

history.event: Initiative created from request, 2026-08-23 PR diagramming memo, and repository survey; intent and shape briefs written.
Question round 1: per-metric + net, treemaps in v1, working-tree default with arbitrary refs. Shape updated: treemap union layout added.
Implementation plan written: CLI payload first (m1), then Explorer (m2), treemap (m3), dependency graph (m4). Headless compare moved from evaluate into m1.

Implemented m1–m4 as stacked PRs #38–#41 on top of docs PR #37. Spikes resolved: snapshot graph identical to in-place (keep cache-dir worktrees); max-weight treemap readable on add-heavy 6687816 (no band fallback). Deviations: treemap tiles use √LOC so small edits stay visible; summed metrics judged like-for-like; compare table redesigned with scorecard, verdicts, inspector at user request.
2026-10-15 voiceover: follow-up compare-ref-picker promotes GitHub PR picking and commit stepping from the cut line.
